questions: Did s-bend finishes rise above 19 of 20, and did line_loss_events fall at or below 0.55?
Did steering_oscillation stay under about 0.35 on the s-bend and oval with mass 0.5? If it rose, is the cause the lower mass or the faster yaw response?
Did the slalom finish any trials, or did its progress rise above 0.26 with line_loss_events below 1.0?
Does the oval still finish 20 of 20 with max_error near 0.017?

If the s-bend holds at its current level and the slalom stays at its max_error floor, is geometry now at its limit, so that the next step should be a controller change (for example kd or kp) rather than more geometry?

intent: Continue the lower-yaw-inertia step that iteration 6 validated. Reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg with body_length held at the 0.10 m minimum and every other geometric value unchanged, so the only change is mass. This should cut yaw inertia by about 17 percent, giving a faster heading response that may push the s-bend to 20 of 20 finishes with line losses at or below 0.55. Oval finishes should stay at 20 of 20. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the s-bend or oval, restore mass to 0.6 kg, since the body length is already at its minimum and the geometry will have reached its limit for this track.
learning: Iteration 6 showed that shortening body_length from 0.12 to 0.10 m at mass 0.6 kg lifted the s-bend to 19 of 20 finishes and the score to 658, with the oval unchanged. Body length is now at its minimum, so mass is the remaining inertia lever. The slalom has not responded to any inertia change (0 finishes in all of iterations 5 and 6), which suggests a separate limit on alternating bends that geometry alone may not solve.
rationale: Iteration 6 (score 657.9, the best so far) kept the 12 mm footprint, y 0.07 layout and wheel_track 0.09, and shortened body_length to 0.10 m at mass 0.6 kg. The s-bend now finishes 19 of 20 (progress 0.996, line losses 0.55, oscillation 0.33), and the oval stays at 20 of 20 with max_error 0.017 and oscillation 0.22. The slalom is unchanged at 0 of 20 finishes, progress 0.26, max_error at the 0.063 floor and oscillation 0.16. Both the s-bend and the oval are well inside the feedback's stated thresholds: s-bend oscillation is 0.33 against a 0.35 limit, so the lower-inertia step is still safe. Following the Integrator's rule, I try mass 0.5 kg with body_length 0.10 m, the next step down in yaw inertia. Body length is already at its 0.10 m minimum, so mass is the only lever left on inertia. Yaw inertia falls from about 0.00122 to about 0.00102 kg·m², roughly 17 percent. Sensor layout, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09, wheel_radius 0.03 and body_width 0.12 stay fixed, so this race isolates mass. Expected result: s-bend finishes at 19 or 20 of 20 with line losses at or below 0.55, and oval finishes stay at 20 of 20. The slalom is probably still limited by turn authority on alternating bends, since it has not responded to inertia changes so far. Risk: oscillation on the s-bend is close to 0.35, so a rise above that is the cue to restore mass to 0.6 and move on to controller work.
